newsitem.title: UK: High-spirited dlr sets new highs against weak mark.
newsitem.headline: High-spirited dlr sets new highs against weak mark.

text.p: The dollar maintained a firm grip on the mark on Tuesday, rising to its highest in almost eight years as dealers bet on Bundesbank reluctance to act to stop the German currency weakening further, analysts said.
The contrast between the robust U.S. economy and its fragile German counterpart continued to drive the dollar higher, they said.
More evidence of German economic problems is expected to come when July unemployment data is released on Wednesday and is expected to show another small rise in jobless queues.
The mark found little comfort in comments from Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing, expressing concern about the pace of the mark's decline.

"There is a sense that the pace of the dollar's rise and the mark's decline is worrying the Bundesbank but as long as it's only expressing concern, there seems to be no holding back on the dollar," said Jeremy Stretch, currency strategist at NatWest Markets in London.

Issing said the exchange rate was one of the most important indicators for the central bank in setting monetary policy. "The fact that the mark has weakened so fast and so significantly certainly gives us something to think about," he said.
In now typical fashion the dollar eased off its highs in the European afternoon in what dealers described as consolidation ahead of the next move higher.

"Dollar/mark's come such a long way, there's the temptation for people to book a bit of profit here as ...it's not very far away from 1.90 marks now," said Pat Magill, head of corporate trading at Daiwa Europe in London.
At 1515 GMT the dollar was at 1.8780/90 marks, down from a high of 1.8820 but up more than a pfennig from 1.8639 in late European trading on Monday.

Dollar/yen was at the mercy of mark/yen, which dropped to two-year lows below 63 yen, amid heavy sales from U.S. funds, before recovering strongly to 63.44/49 in late trade here. Dollar/yen was at 119.07, up from 118.22.

The dollar also set a fresh near-four high against the Swiss franc at 1.5365 before easing to 1.5315/25 in late trade. Against the French franc it rose to its highest since October 1989 at 6.3507 before easing to 6.3375/95.

A warning shot came from Willi Leibfritz, economist at Germany's Ifo research institute, who said dollar gains above 1.90 marks would "set alarm bells ringing in Frankfurt" and prompt the Bundesbank to take action.

Expectatations that the Bundesbank will allow the repo rate to drift higher have intensified as the mark slid nearly eight percent against the dollar in the past month alone and tumbled to five-year lows in trade-weighted terms.
Some traders speculate that the central bank will switch to variable rate repos soon to allow the repo rate to drift up from a record low of 3.0 percent.
But foreign exchange analysts doubted whether the Bundesbank had much scope to reverse the weak mark trend. Sustained rate rises would threaten to stop the recovering German economy in its tracks.
Moreover, the knock-on effect on other European economies which would have to follow suit would be devastating, analysts said.

"The Bundesbank has little room for manoeuvre to counteract the weakness of the mark and as soon as they switch to setting variable rate repos, they will have shot all their ammunition," said Brian Martin, currency strategist at BZW in London.
The dollar/mark rally and firm UK July output data energised sterling to rise above 3.06 marks before easing to 3.0560/70.
Speculation that UK interest rates will be raised at the meeting of the Bank of England's monetary policy committee on Wednesday and Thursday kept buoying the pound, traders said.
UK industrial output rose a higher-than-forecast 1.4 percent in June from July. -- London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
